Kentrell Lang arrested on charges of intimidating witnesses in Napoleonville
M. S. Hollis
Kentrell Lang, 46, of 212 Telegraph St., Napoleonville, was arrested on Aug. 12 on multiple felony charges after allegedly attempting to intimidate, harass, or threaten witnesses associated with an ongoing criminal trial.
Assumption Parish Sheriff Leland Falcon said deputies responded Wednesday morning to an incident near the location where court proceedings were scheduled to begin involving Lang. According to the sheriff's office, Lang made loud verbal comments directed at individuals connected to the trial. The comments were considered intimidating, threatening, or harassing.
Following the incident, deputies arrested and booked Lang into the Assumption Parish Detention Center. He faces five counts of intimidating, impeding, or injuring witnesses or officers and one count of resisting an officer.
Lang remains incarcerated pending a bond hearing. The sheriff’s office has provided contact information for further inquiries regarding this case: Sheriff Leland Falcon or Public Information Officer Lonny Cavalier can be reached at (985) 498-9353 or (985) 369-2912.
No additional details about the ongoing criminal trial or those involved have been released by authorities.
